subject: Dedicated fleet intake — token-flow & session-shape checklist
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Jordan <ajordan@cerebralabs.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@cerebralabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2029 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated fleet intake — token-flow & session-shape checklist

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks for taking the time yesterday. To get our pre-sales sizing spot-on for the Dedicated deployment, could you fill in a few focused datapoints so we can map to a recommended GPU mix and initial commit? If easier, the two attached files are an editable CSV + a short prompt sample to drop values into. High-level items we need: 

- Typical concurrent sessions (baseline) and observed peak concurrency (15-min and 1-min peaks).
- Average prompt length (tokens) and average model-generated response length (tokens) — p50/p95 if available.
- Session duration (median / typical conversation length), and whether sessions are interactive chat (multiple turn stateful) or stateless one-shot calls.
- Percent split by workload type: chat/generation/embeddings/reranking.
- Expected SLA (p95 latency target) and acceptable queueing window (e.g., can you tolerate 200–500ms extra during a 90th percentile burst?).
- Desired model family(s) (open Llama, Falcon-xx, or customer-provided) and tolerance for quantized variants.
- Daily token volume estimate and expected month-over-month growth (if known).
- Any requirements for data residency / VPC or air-gapped deployment.

If you can paste a small representative sample (10–50 requests) or attach an aggregate CSV (timestamp, arrival_ms, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, session_id), that will speed things up.

Goal: with these, we'll produce a concise recommended fleet (SKU mix, KV cache sizing, suggested batch sizes, canary fractions) and a preliminary cost/throughput projection.

Appreciate it — we can iterate quickly once we have the traffic sample.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
lukas@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: cerebra_traffic_sample_template.csv (stub), example_prompt_set.txt (stub)
From: Alex Jordan <ajordan@cerebralabs.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@cerebralabs.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2029 16:12:08 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated fleet intake — token-flow & session-shape checklist

Hi Lukas / Marissa,

Thanks — attaching the CSV export you requested (cerebra_traffic_sample.csv). Quick answers up-front to save time: 

- Baseline concurrent sessions: ~220 steady; typical 15-min peak: 1,180; 1-min instantaneous top-out we've seen at 1,450 during campaign spikes.
- Prompt lengths (tokens): avg prompt 38 tokens (p95 140).
- Response lengths (tokens): avg response 210 tokens (p95 980 for long-form summaries).
- Session shape: 62% multi-turn chat (stateful, we expect KV-cache reuse across turns), 28% single-shot generation, 5% embeddings, 5% reranking.
- Median session duration: ~42s; active-turn cadence ~3–4 turns per session.
- SLA target: p95 end-to-end inference latency <= 450ms for chat endpoints; for batch/embeddings we can tolerate higher. During large marketing bursts we can accept up to ~1s p95 if necessary, but prefer graceful degradation not hard failure.
- Model family: primary is open-weight Falcon-180B (we currently use a distilled variant); we're open to quantized 8-bit variants if perf/quality tradeoff is acceptable.
- Daily token estimate: today ~42M tokens; projected ~25% QoQ growth.
- Residency: US-only production, but control plane can be hosted.

Let me know if you need specific example prompts (I attached example_prompt_set.txt). Happy to jump on a quick screen share to walk through the CSV.

Thanks,
Alex Jordan
Head of ML Platforms, Cerebra Labs
ajordan@cerebralabs.com

Attachment: cerebra_traffic_sample.csv (stub)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Jordan <ajordan@cerebralabs.com>

Date: Tue, 23 Jul 2029 08:47:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated fleet intake — token-flow & session-shape checklist

Alex — quick clarifiers that will materially change the sizing run: 

1) When you say p95 response 980 tokens for long-form summaries, how frequent are those? (e.g., 0.5% of requests, 5% of requests?)
2) For the Falcon-180B usage: are you able to accept an 8-bit-quantized runtime for non-critical endpoints (e.g., asynchronous summaries) or do you require FP16 across the board?
3) Any planned marketing/holiday windows in next 90 days that could create >2x historic peak? If so, what lead time do you have for notifications?

If you can answer those three points we can lock an initial Dedicated SKU mix. We'll draft a 30/60/90 canary plan with a fall-back to a smaller hosted variant to avoid blackouts.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Jordan <ajordan@cerebralabs.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jul 2029 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated fleet intake — token-flow & session-shape checklist

Alex / team — thanks for the CSV and prompt samples. High-level initial sizing recommendation based on the provided traffic: 

Summary numbers we used: baseline concurrency 220, 15-min peak 1,180, 1-min peak 1,450; avg prompt 38 tokens / avg response 210 tokens; daily tokens ~42M; 62% stateful chat.

Preliminary Dedicated footprint (proposal):
- GPU mix: 6 x A100-80GB (for peak CT-heavy chat lanes with KV cache residency) + 4 x A40-equivalent (for async summaries, reranking, and lower priority generation). This gives room for ~1.1–1.3k concurrent chat-heavy connections at p95 with conservative batching.
- KV cache sizing: plan for ~120GB total in-GPU KV reservation to keep hot session contexts resident (we'll pin the hottest 20% of sessions, fallback to local host memory for cold sessions).
- Batching & latency: suggest dynamic batching up to 24 tokens/time-slice for chat lanes and larger batch windows for async jobs. Targeted p95 latency headroom: 400–450ms for chat when running at planned throughput.
- Canary/fallback: start with 30% traffic to Dedicated (canary) for 72 hours, ramp 30->60->100 with automated rollback criteria on p95 latency and error-rate. Maintain a hosted fallback pool sized to absorb 20% of traffic if Dedicated experiences capacity events.
- Cost & ops note: preliminary monthly inference cost estimate (infra + per-token ops) ~ $37k–$48k depending on quantization acceptance. If Cerebra accepts 8-bit quant for the async summary endpoint, we can reduce GPU count by ~1 A100-equiv and lower cost ~12%.

Action items: 
- Alex: confirm what percent of requests fall into the p95 980-token bucket (Marissa Q1).
- Alex / Priya: confirm quantization tolerance for non-time-critical endpoints.
- Lukas / Marissa: I'll produce a tighter SKU-level proposal with expected throughput per node, expected queueing at p95, and suggested autoscale ranges.

I'll attach a short spreadsheet with per-GPU throughput estimates in a follow-up. Happy to set a 30-minute call to walk through the trade-offs tomorrow.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Infrastructure Reliability, Redwood Inference
dev@redwoodinference.com

Attachments referenced: preliminary-sizing-summary.xlsx (to follow)
